jobs.description:
Join LOCA – gastronomy, hospitality and sustainability

LOCA Group is looking for talented and passionate Chefs and Sous Chefs to join our restaurants in Copenhagen.
At LOCA, we work with something we believe is one of the most important things in the world: the meal. We believe gastronomy can help create a better future, and every day we work to combine high gastronomic standards, genuine hospitality and concrete sustainable choices. 
For us, sustainability starts with the ingredient. We work with seasonal produce, high levels of organic ingredients, local producers and reducing food waste. 
We want to raise the bar for how sustainability is approached in gastronomy – without compromising flavour or the guest experience.

We are looking for Chefs and Sous ChefsWe are looking for both experienced Chefs and Sous Chefs who want to become part of our different kitchens.We are looking for people who:

• 
Are trained Chefs or have equivalent relevant experience

• 
Have experience from professional kitchens with high gastronomic standards.

• 
Work in a structured way and remain calm and focused during service.

• 
Have strong culinary skills and a genuine passion for gastronomy.

• 
Enjoy teamwork and contribute positively to the kitchen environment.

• 
Are curious and motivated to develop both professionally and personally.

• 
Have an interest in sustainability, organic ingredients, seasonal produce and local producers.

• 
For Sous Chef positions, you should also have experience with leadership, planning, ordering, food safety and the daily operation of a professional kitchen.

We value respect, collaboration, responsibility and the desire to keep improving.

Our restaurants

As part of LOCA, you will have the opportunity to work in different gastronomic environments:

Amélie – The Opera House
A modern Danish brasserie where classic French techniques meet Danish ingredients and the unique atmosphere of the Opera House. The kitchen works across à la carte, opera service and larger events
.PAULA – Carlsberg Byen
A modern French-Japanese kitchen focusing on deep umami, precision, seasonal ingredients and a minimum of 60% organic produce. A small, focused team with high gastronomic ambitions.
DOLORES – Carlsberg Byen
A vibrant restaurant inspired by San Francisco’s Mission District, serving creative sharing-style dishes with seasonal ingredients in a relaxed atmosphere.
Restaurant RADIO – Frederiksberg
A modern Nordic restaurant with more than 15 years of history. The restaurant focuses on organic and seasonal ingredients, local producers, vegetables and fish from Nordic waters.LOCA also operates
Kilden i Haven in Tivoli and several canteens.

What we offer

• 
A workplace with high gastronomic ambitions.

• 
An international and diverse working environment.

• 
Passionate and dedicated colleagues.

• 
Opportunities for professional and personal development.

• 
Responsibility and influence in your daily work.

• 
Opportunities for further training and development within LOCA.

• 
Salary and employment conditions based on qualifications.

• 
The opportunity to become part of a company actively working to shape the future of sustainable gastronomy.

Why LOCA?We believe the best restaurants are created by people who want to succeed together.At LOCA, you are not simply joining a kitchen. You become part of a community where we share knowledge, support each other and work together to create great meals and great workplaces.We believe Every Meal Matters – and that the choices we make today help create a better world tomorrow.Practical information

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark

Employment: Full-time

Positions: Chef / Sous Chef

Start: By agreement / as soon as possible

Salary: Based on qualifications

Interviews are conducted on an ongoing basis.
If you would like to join LOCA, please send your CV and application telling us a little about yourself, your experience and why you would like to work with us.Send your resume to job@locarestauranter.dk

jobs.occupation: Are you our new GTM Engineer?
jobs.description:
About the Role

In this cross-functional, individual-contributor role, you will build, operate, and iterate Accutics' GTM revenue system across the entire sales lifecycle: Accounts → contacts → signals → outreach → meetings → pipeline → revenue → expansion.

You will not only be responsible for filling the funnel; you will own the systems, data, routing, and operational efficiency to ensure a seamless handoff, maximum conversion velocity, and a reliable path from activity to revenue using a modern GTM stack (Clay, Claude Code/Codex, Instantly, HeyReach, ...).

You will work side-by-side with our AEs, Product Marketer, and CPO, and report directly to the CEO. This is a hands-on role for a technical self-starter who builds things themselves, takes ownership, experiments quickly, and turns successful tests into production systems.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead Generation & Demand Capture: Build, operate, and iterate targeted, multi-channel campaigns across outbound, ABM, and account expansion to generate qualified meetings, pipeline, and revenue. Build account/contact lists, enrich prospects, identify signals, and activate contacts through appropriate channels.

• Sales Enablement & Alignment: Act as a GTM systems partner to the sales team. Deliver well-qualified accounts and contacts equipped with deep contextual data, signals, and account intelligence. Onboard sales reps into workflows and ensure system transparency so it saves them time rather than becoming a black box.

• AI-Supported Revenue Operations: Build and operate the GTM technology and data stack. Build robust enrichment, scoring, routing, synchronization, and automation workflows.

• Market & Persona Strategy: Translate ICP, enterprise account, and persona strategies into repeatable GTM workflows and continuously iterate based on performance.

• Flawless Tracking: “Drink our own champagne.” Utilize the Accutics platform internally to guarantee that our own campaign tracking, naming conventions, and metadata are perfectly structured from the point of creation. Maintain high-quality GTM and CRM data so pipeline and revenue can be reliably measured.

• Full-Funnel Analytics: Monitor the GTM system and its commercial performance from initial account targeting through closed-won revenue and account expansion. Identify bottlenecks and build solutions to fix them.

What We Are Looking For

Required:

· Enterprise GTM Execution: 1–3 years of hands-on experience in GTM Engineering, GTM Operations, or RevOps, preferably in GTM agency or B2B SaaS. Proven track record taking outbound, ABM, and expansion campaigns from concept to production.

· GTM Engineering & Data: Hands-on experience with Clay (including Function and Workflow capabilities), bidirectional CRM sync with Salesforce, APIs, webhooks, and automation workflow logic.

· AI / Agentic GTM: Experience experimenting with and deploying production multi-agent GTM systems built with Claude Code, Codex, or similar tools.

· Working Style: Highly autonomous, operationally disciplined, and commercially minded, measuring success by quality pipeline and revenue, not top-of-funnel metrics.

A Plus:

· Experience with GTM tools such as email and LinkedIn sequencers, unified inboxes, email infrastructure, enrichment, intent/signal, LinkedIn social warming, call dialer.

· Experience building other GTM workflows: account expansion/ churn/ partner sales/ inbound flywheel.

· Experience building Salesforce CRM data foundation, CRM data cleaning routines for modern GTM.

· Comfortable handling SQL, Agent loops.

What We Offer

· Ownership: Build, operate, and iterate Accutics' new GTM revenue system across the sales lifecycle.

· Modern Stack: Hands-on experience with Clay, Claude Code/Codex, Instantly, HeyReach, ...

· Commercial Impact: Direct impact on pipeline generation, deal velocity, and revenue while returning time to sales teams.

· Agile Environment: Small, international SaaS team with high autonomy, short decision paths, and direct leadership access.

· Copenhagen Office: Central Copenhagen location, Nordic work-life balance, flexible hours, and regular social events.

· Package: Permanent full-time position, competitive salary, pension, and benefits.

Requirements

• You have a valid work permit to work in Europe (Denmark).

• You are fluent in English, both verbally and in writing.

• You are located in the Greater Copenhagen Area (Denmark) or will be relocating here.

Hiring Process

1. GTM Builder Interview: Meet a GTM builder and demonstrate systems you have built and deployed.

2. CEO Interview: Discuss Accutics, the role, and how you will shape the GTM engine.

3. Build Together Session: Collaboratively solve a real GTM challenge to demonstrate your build and testing approach.

What Success Looks Like (3-6 Months)

· Take full build and iteration responsibility for Accutics' GTM revenue system.

· Establish and run daily operational routines, onboarding sales reps to maintain workflow transparency.

· Bring the Salesforce data foundation up to the standard of your new GTM system.

· Continuously test new tools, workflows, and solutions to eliminate sales friction and deliver quality pipeline and revenue.

About Accutics

Accutics is a Copenhagen-based B2B SaaS company providing the ultimate data foundation for global enterprise marketing. We work with the world’s leading brands. Our platform standardizes campaign tracking, governs taxonomy, and ensures data is AI-ready, eliminating manual QA loops for confident, data-informed decisions.

Proud of our Nordic roots, we combine deep domain expertise with close collaboration. We are a small, international team looking for a GTM Engineer to build, operate, and continuously improve a modern, AI-native revenue system across the entire funnel.

How to Apply

Think you’re the right fit? Apply today by submitting your resume and a brief cover letter. You can email it to careers@accutics.com.

Would you like to help build and develop the platform that makes it easier for Whiteaway’s software Engineers to develop, deploy and run their solutions?

Whiteaway Group is looking for a skilled Platform Engineer to join their Platform Squad in Aarhus.

As a Platform Engineer, you will become part of a strong technical environment focused on building and continuously improving the platform used by Whiteaway’s development teams in their daily work.

This is not traditional IT operations. Instead, the focus is on creating automated, stable and scalable solutions that make it easier for Engineers to develop, deploy and run their software.

Whiteaway is a digital-first company where technology plays a central role in the business. The company operates some of the largest online stores in the Nordics within electronics and home appliances, and its technical platforms are an important part of the continued development of the business.

Your role

You will play a central role in developing and improving Whiteaway’sinternal platform and will work closely with software Engineers and the other members of the Platform Squad.

A key part of the role is the close collaboration with Engineers. You will be curious about how they work, understand their needs and challenges, and use their feedback to identify how workflows, processes and platform tooling can be made simpler, faster and better.

Over the coming years, Whiteaway will be taking the platform to a significantly higher level. A key focus will be reducing and removing legacy and building a more modern, scalable and developer-friendly platform. AI will also play an increasingly important role in how the platform develops and how Whiteaway’s Engineers work.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Developing and continuously improving the cloud platform

• Automating deployment and development processes

• Infrastructure as Code

• CI/CD pipelines

• Containerisation and Kubernetes

• Cloud infrastructure – primarily AWS

• Monitoring, observability and reliability

• Engineering tooling and self-service solutions

• Security and access management

• Troubleshooting and optimising platform performance and stability

The role offers a high degree of freedom, and you will have the opportunity to take ownership and influence both the technology and the way the team works.

Whiteaway believes in freedom under responsibility. You will have the opportunity to take ownership, influence technical decisions and help shape both the platform and the way the team works.

We imagine that you…

You have a strong technical background and experience within software development, cloud, DevOps or platform engineering. Perhaps you are already working as a Platform Engineer, Cloud Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer or Senior Software Engineer with strong cloud and infrastructure experience.

Your title is less important than your motivation to work hands-on with platform engineering and your ability to thrive at the intersection of software development, cloud and operations. Experience with general software development is an advantage, particularly Node.js and/or Go.

We would like you to have experience with several of the following technologies and tools:

• AWS

• Kubernetes

• Docker

• Terraform / Infrastructure as Code

• CI/CD

• Git/GitHub

• Linux

• Node.js and/or Go

• Datadog

• ArgoCD

• Spacelift

• Cloudflare

• Monitoring and observability

• Networking and cloud infrastructure

Experience with GitOps is an advantage, but not a requirement. Experience with security or with the intersection between operations and software development is also considered an advantage.

You do not need to know everything. What matters most is that you have strong technical curiosity, can understand complex problems and are motivated to continuously improve the way things are done.

Your professional development is important to Whiteaway.

You will have the opportunity to work with development plans, strengthen your technical skills and take your expertise to the next level. At the same time, knowledge sharing is an important part of the culture – you are expected not only to develop yourself, but also to help lift others around you.

On a personal level, drive, determination and humility are highly valued. You take ownership and get things done, while remaining curious, collaborative and motivated to find the best solutions together with others.

What Whiteaway offers

At Whiteaway, you will be part of an informal, inclusive and supportive leadership culture where Engineers have real ownership and the opportunity to influence their work. The culture is built around experimentation, knowledge sharing and continuous learning, with opportunities to take part in hackathons, pair programming and MOB programming, as well as access to learning resources.

The social side of working together is also important. People at Whiteaway genuinely enjoy working together, and there is a strong focus on building good relationships across the team. Through activities such as hackathons, Improvement Mondays and other social initiatives, there are plenty of opportunities to come together, share knowledge, experiment and have fun.

Whiteaway also values a healthy work-life balance, a great lunch and good colleagues. The office is located in Skejby, with free parking.

About Whiteaway Group

Whiteaway Group is a tribe of 300+ passionate people working across Scandinavia, selling and shipping appliances through e-commerce, franchise stores and B2B channels.

Around 250 employees are based at the headquarters in Aarhus, covering the group’s central functions. Around 45 people work within Tech across IT, Engineering and Product. The Platform Squad currently consists of four Platform Engineers, and the team is expected to grow in the coming years as the demands on and use of the platform continue to increase – including with the growing use of AI.

With brands like Skousen, Tretti and Whiteaway, the group is grounded in innovation and honesty, always pushing for better customer experiences through technology.

Interested in joining Whiteaway Group?

Bloom is handling the recruitment process on behalf of Whiteaway Group and is actively reviewing applications. We look forward to receiving your application and CV in Danish or English as soon as possible.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact IT Recruitment Manager Dorte Pape at Bloom at dp@bloom.dk or on +45 3160 9365.

Building AI keeps getting cheaper and faster. Deciding what's worth building, and getting an organisation to actually commit to it, does not.

At Heyra, we build AI systems, workflows and data platforms that are meant to live in production from day one. We work closely with companies that are moving quickly and need a partner who can hold both the strategic picture and the delivery reality in one head.

We're looking for a Deployment Strategist: the person the client's leadership talks to. You own the relationship and the outcome. You sit with a C-suite buyer, understand where their business is actually trying to go, and translate that into a sharp, sequenced plan for what we build and why. Then you steer a strong engineering team to make it real - without being the one in the codebase.

This is the strategic counterpart to our engineers. Where they go deep into the build, you hold the commercial and strategic frame: what problem are we really solving, what impact are we creating, in what order, and how do we get the organisation to adopt it. You're more product manager than a traditional consultant, with a strong strategic angle - closer to an Engagement Manager who's technical enough to make the right calls than a slide-deck advisor.

You'll work closely with engineers, data specialists, strategists and designers in a company where ideas move quickly and the distance from thinking to building is intentionally small.

What you'll work on

• 
Owning client relationships at the leadership level - being the person the C-suite trusts

• 
Framing the real problem behind the ask, and shaping it into an engagement worth running together with our FDEs

• 
Sequencing what gets built, in what order, and being accountable for the business value - not just the artifact

• 
Steering engineering teams toward outcomes, translating in both directions between the client and the builders

• 
Driving adoption: managing expectations, working with the people who have to live with the solution, and staying through the part after launch

• 
Scoping, structuring and de-risking engagements as they evolve

• 
Spotting where the next opportunity sits inside an account and growing it

Requirements

You probably have experience with

• 
Management consulting, change management, adoption, implementation of AI-native solutions.

• 
Owning client or stakeholder relationships end to end, with real accountability for outcomes

• 
Product, programme or engagement leadership in a technical environment

• 
Being technically literate - fluent enough in data and AI to make the right calls and earn trust with both buyers and builders, without needing to write the production code yourself

• 
Translating between business strategy and what's actually buildable

• 
Bringing structure to ambiguous, fast-moving situations

• 
The patience to sit with a worried manager, and the stubbornness to stay until adoption actually lands

Curiosity, taste and the way you think matter just as much to us as specific tools or years of experience. We hire for the who, not the what - experience is an indicator of perspective, not a deciding factor for how senior a role you'll play here. We're hiring across levels and shape the role around the person.

Why Heyra

At Heyra, we believe consulting needs to be rewritten. We're building a consultancy designed for the agentic era. We design, build, and operate AI products that change how enterprises work - from problem to prototype to production.

We care deeply about craft, speed and building things that work in the real world.

Heyra brings together people from engineering, strategy, product, startup and creative environments. We keep teams small, collaboration close and momentum high.

You'll join a team where:

people care deeply about what they build

good ideas move quickly

new technology gets explored early

and where there is room to shape both the company and the way we work

We're around 50 people today after merging with Pyne, and we're only just getting started.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

Veo's security surface is unusual. You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across platform security, identity, and network security, and rolling out the first paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, CVE response, CI/CD identity, and a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen). • Work with the auth service maintainers on identity and access, including MFA rollouts, removal of shared accounts, and cleanup of long-lived tokens, so the patterns stay theirs to own

• Make workload identity the paved road for CI/CD, using OIDC between GitHub Actions and AWS or GCP, packaged so teams can migrate themselves

• Mentor the rest of the team and raise the security bar across Builders

As the team matures, you will help shape our multi-environment network architecture, our identity and access patterns, and the long-term security posture of the product.

What You Could Bring

This is a deliberately merged platform security and identity role. You do not need to be world class at both. You likely have several years of production infrastructure and security experience behind you, and you are deep and credible in one of these areas and ready to grow into the other.

That depth tends to show up in several of the following:

Nice to have: GitOps tools such as Flux or ArgoCD, Cilium, Kubernetes security at scale, and experience building security into a GRC evidence pipeline.

How We Work

You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy, and Environmental Medicine at the Department of Public Health, Faculty of Health, University of Southern Denmark, is offering a new 5-year (20%) position for an Associate Professor within clinical pharmacy. The position is to be filled from February 1st, 2027.

The academic position

The research areas of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine (CPPEM) span from pharmacological epidemiology to clinical studies and cell-based basic pharmacology. CPPEM has a strong background in investigations of exposure to environmental chemicals, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacogenetics, pharmacokinetics, drug-drug interactions, and therapeutic drug monitoring. The academic position is affiliated with the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, that utilizes the Danish registries to assess pharmacological questions in large populations. 

The area of research is flexible within the area of pharmacoepidemiologic and clinical research and could be (but is not limited to) drug use patterns and rational pharmacotherapy. The department has a strong focus on interdisciplinary collaboration both in-house and with external researchers and the new person is expected to continue this tradition.
 

Areas of responsibility

The applicant will be expected to establish their own research area within the pharmacoepidemiologic research group at the department. Thus, the applicant should be able to attract external research funding to support research and employ scientific and technical staff. The applicant may have a background within pharmacy or medicine.

The research unit teaches in four educations: Medicine, Pharmacy, Chiropractor, and Biomedicine, and the position comes with teaching obligations within these subjects at the University as well as supervision of bachelor and master projects. Additionally, we expect that you will contribute to administrative duties, e.g., participating in Study Board or other similar activities. 

Fluent English (both written and spoken) is required. You are expected to have qualifications that renders it probable that you will be able to establish your own research area within the research unit. Further, you are required to have a PhD degree or similar research experience. 
 

Employers

Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine today has approximately 50 employees. It consists of three separate research groups: pharmacoepidemiology, translational pharmacology, and environmental medicine. Additionally, it collaborates closely with the Department of Pharmacology at OUH. Collectively, this constitutes Denmark’s largest center for research, teaching and clinical service in pharmacology.

It produces approximately 100 international peer-reviewed publications per year. 

Professor Tore B. Stage heads the unit and Professor Pernille Tanggaard Andersen heads the Department.

Management

The Associate Professor answers to the research leader for the unit of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine.
 

Contact information

Further information can be obtained from the leader for the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, Professor Anton Pottegård (apottegaard@health.sdu.dk).
 

Application deadline and interviews

November 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CET
 

Salary and terms of employment

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Applications will be assessed by an expert committee. Applicants will be informed of their assessment by the university.

Applications – including the required attachments – must be sent via the below-mentioned link “Apply online". Only online applications will be accepted. Attached files must be Adobe PDF or Word format. Each field in the application form can contain up to max. 10 MB.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.
 

Application (as pdf- or Word/docx- files):

• 
a motivation letter

a detailed CV

degree certificates (inclusive of PhD diploma)

a complete and numbered list of publications

• 
10 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please notice that one pdf- or docx- file must be attached for each publication

a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

a research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

The Ravnskjaer lab at the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit, Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark, invites applications from outstanding candidates who are interested in joining our team as PhD fellow. The position is available from December 1, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

 

The Ravnskjaer lab is headed by Assoc. Prof. Kim Ravnskjaer and focuses on the molecular basis for cardiometabolic health. We combine comprehensive studies of human biopsies with targeted gene disruption in advanced preclinical models, single cell transcriptomics, and bioimaging. Expertise in wet-lab and computational biology, close ties to the clinic, and a wonderful team of early career scientists give us the agility to swiftly move from hypotheses to biological insights and mechanism.

Our lab is based in the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit, which constitutes an international, ambitious, dynamic, and well-resourced working environment. Our unit and department have state-of-the-art facilities for flow cytometry, next generation sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, mass spectrometry, metabolomics, bioimaging, and transgenic mouse work. Strategic research alliances exist with regional hospitals including Odense University Hospital (OUH).

 

We are partners in several regional, national and international initiatives including the DNRF-funded Center for Functional Genomics and Tissue Plasticity aimed at obtaining systems-level, mechanistic and cell type-resolved understanding of tissue plasticities in diet-induced obesity and regression.

For the current project, Molecular Determinants of Adipose Tissue Lipoprotein Clearance, we seek an experimentalist with hands-on experience in adipose tissue or microvascular biology, FELASA B certification or similar, working experience with mouse models, and as well as an interest in lipid metabolism. Familiarity with adipose tissue imaging techniques is an advantage.

 

We offer:

• 
A three-year PhD position (or four-year for Master students) in a supportive, stimulating, and interdisciplinary research environment

• 
Enrollment in PhD school of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, which allows the candidate to tailor a flexible individualized course program

• 
Training in a wide range of scientific and transferable skills including research management, communication, networking, presentations, writing of manuscripts etc.

• 
Mentoring and career development in a network of national and international collaborators

• 
Research exchange to collaborating institutions, depending on the project and interest of the PhD student

• 
Access to state-of-the-art equipment, workflows, and infrastructure

• 
Competitive salary and social benefits (health coverage, parental leave, social security etc.)

• 
Dedicated assistance and support with various practical, social, and legal aspects, especially for international candidates through our international staff office (ISO) and department

 

Qualifications/requirements
We are looking for highly motivated, dedicated, and ambitious candidates with:

• 
A Master’s degree in Life Science, preferable Molecular Biology, Biomedicine, or Computational Systems Biology. If you have not yet completed your master program, you can apply to be enrolled in our 4+4 PhD program, which is a way to commence the PhD study whilst concurrently completing the master program (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om_sdu/sdus_profil/strategi/udfolder_talenter_og_fremmer_det_unikke/4_plus_4_ph_d)

• 
Strong collaborative and communication skills and an interest in working in an interdisciplinary environment

• 
Proficiency in spoken and written English

• 
Documented hands-on experience with liver biology, cell culture and mouse physiology is considered an advantage.

 

Application deadline: 27. October 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time
